q: The internal energy of a body is the sum of the total kinetic energy and potential energy of the molecules.
e: True. The internal energy of a body is the sum of the total kinetic energy and potential energy of the molecules. Kinetic energy is ½mv². It is the energy of motion.

q: The internal energy of a body is the sum of the total kinetic energy and potential energy of the atoms.
e: False. The claim puts atoms where molecules belongs. The internal energy of a body is the sum of the total kinetic energy and potential energy of the molecules. Kinetic energy is ½mv².

q: The kinetic energy of molecules is energy due to their motions.
e: True. The kinetic energy of molecules is energy due to their motions. Kinetic energy is ½mv². It is the energy of motion.

q: The kinetic energy is directly related to temperature.
e: True. The kinetic energy is directly related to temperature. Kinetic energy is ½mv². It is the energy of motion.

q: The rise in temperature of a substance is due to an increase in the average kinetic energy of the molecules.
e: True. The rise in temperature of a substance is due to an increase in the average kinetic energy of the molecules. Kinetic energy is ½mv². It is the energy of motion.

q: The potential energy is energy due to inter-molecular forces between the molecules.
e: True. The potential energy is energy due to inter-molecular forces between the molecules. Internal energy is the molecules' kinetic energy plus the potential energy from their spacing.

q: The magnitude of potential energy stored depends on the distance between the molecules (or) the particles in that substance.
e: True. The magnitude of potential energy stored depends on the distance between the molecules (or) the particles in that substance. Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts.

q: The internal energy of the substance is known as its thermal energy.
e: True. The internal energy of the substance is known as its thermal energy. Internal energy is the molecules' kinetic energy plus the potential energy from their spacing.

q: The transfer of thermal energy from one substance to another is referred to as heat.
e: True. The transfer of thermal energy from one substance to another is referred to as heat. Heat is energy flowing because of a temperature difference. SI unit is the joule.

q: When an object at a certain temperature is placed in contact with another object at a higher temperature, the thermal energy (heat) is transferred from the object at a lower temperature to one at a higher temperature.
e: False. Heat is energy flowing because of a temperature difference. SI unit is the joule.
